Each link below was checked this session and loads.

- **[21 CFR 606.100 — Cornell Legal Information Institute](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/606.100)**
  — the SOP-requirement regulation, including paragraph (b)'s clause on written procedures for
  product-deviation investigations, quoted in this lesson. The local verbatim copy used here lives
  at `sources/cfr/606.100.md`.

- **[21 CFR 606.171 — Cornell Legal Information Institute](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/606.171)**
  — the biological product deviation reporting rule this lesson applies to Owen Pruitt's donation.
  Already the full subject of the `risk-and-controls-vocabulary` foundation lesson; use this as a
  stable, citable mirror of the same text. Local copy: `sources/cfr/606.171.md`.

- **[21 CFR 630.10 — Cornell Legal Information Institute](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/630.10)**
  — general donor eligibility requirements, including paragraph (h) (must not collect from a
  deferred donor) and the travel-history eligibility factor in paragraph (e)(2)(iii), both quoted
  or cited in this lesson. Local copy: `sources/cfr/630.10.md`.

- **[GovInfo: Code of Federal Regulations collection](https://www.govinfo.gov/app/collection/cfr)**
  — the U.S. Government Publishing Office's official CFR collection, useful as a fallback primary
  source if a specific eCFR or Cornell page is ever unreachable, and for pulling an official PDF of
  a full CFR part when you need one for the record.

- **[Deviation Investigation in the Pharmaceutical Industry](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ukeUUiZ0Sc8)**
  (GMP-SOP Videos, from oEmbed `author_name`) — the video embedded in this lesson. A GMP/pharma-
  industry educational channel walking through deviation investigation generally: discovery,
  containment, root cause, disposition, closure. It won't name 606.171, 630.10(h), or Lakeshore's
  facts — it's the broader pharmaceutical-GMP version of the exact five-stage process this lesson
  teaches for blood establishments specifically, worth seeing once from outside the blood-specific
  lens. Verified embeddable via YouTube oEmbed on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[Quality-One: RCA — Root Cause Analysis](https://quality-one.com/rca/)** — a quality-engineering
  consultancy's explainer on root-cause-analysis methods generally, including 5 Why and the
  Fishbone (Ishikawa) diagram, the two tools stage 3's impact assessment draws on without this
  lesson re-deriving them. Use this before running a real root-cause session on a CAPA-bound
  deviation like Owen Pruitt's. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[ICH Q9: Quality Risk Management](https://database.ich.org/sites/default/files/Q9_Guideline.pdf)**
  — the International Council for Harmonisation's guideline on quality risk management (this is the
  original Step 4 text dated 9 November 2005, not ICH's 2023 Q9(R1) revision — no verified-loading
  link to the R1 text was found this session), the industry-standard framework behind the
  likelihood/severity/detectability reasoning this lesson's stage 3 applies (and the
  `risk-and-controls-vocabulary` foundation first taught). ICH Q9 is guidance adopted across FDA,
  EMA, and other regulators — not an FDA regulation and not an AABB Standard, so label it
  accordingly if it comes up in a real document. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11
  (HTTP 200, confirmed as a 23-page PDF).

- **[TapRooT: Root Cause Analysis Tip — Extent of Cause … Extent of
  Condition](https://taproot.com/?p=105731)** — a root-cause-analysis training firm's explainer on
  extent-of-condition specifically: the "what else does this touch" question stage 3 asks about
  Brookfield's other donors and other satellite sites, distinguished from extent-of-cause (whether
  the root cause itself needs deeper generic-cause analysis). Useful for seeing the concept argued
  on its own terms, independent of this lesson's blood-industry framing. Verified loading via `curl`
  on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

## Keep learning

Not official sources — good places to learn more about handling deviations and investigating them.

- **[Deviation Management Process In GMP](https://gmpinsiders.com/deviation-management-process/)** (GMP Insiders, practitioner site) — Walks through logging, classifying, investigating and closing deviations, including the common trap of stopping at 'operator error'. Any timelines it quotes are one site's example, not a rule. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
- **[Corrective and preventive action](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corrective_and_preventive_action)** (Wikipedia) — A neutral overview of how deviations feed into CAPA, useful as a bridge to the next module. Page title checked: "Corrective and preventive action - Wikipedia". Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
- **[5 Whys: Finding the Root Cause](https://www.ihi.org/library/tools/5-whys-finding-root-cause)** (Institute for Healthcare Improvement) — A free healthcare-quality tool page with a worked example; good for practising the investigation habit on a deviation. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
